newsitem.title: UK: CalEnergy says Pru buy talk "extraordinary".
newsitem.headline: CalEnergy says Pru buy talk "extraordinary".

text.p: U.S. utility CalEnergy, which controls CE Electric -- the hostile bidder for Northern Electric -- said on Tuesday reports of Prudential Corp buying Northern shares were "extraordinary".

"If these reports of the Prudential trying to buy shares in the market are true, it raises all sorts of questions about their motives and, quite frankly, is extraordinary," a CalEnergy spokesman said in an interview.
Talk buzzed among dealers that Northern's key institutional investor was in the market on Tuesday trying to buy Northern shares in an effort to defeat the 782 million stg takeover.

Industry sources said there was market speculation that the Prudential had been trying to persuade traders who have conditionally pledged their shares to CE Electric, to instead sell to the Prudential -- for the same 650p-per-share -- when the temporarily suspended stock resumed trade on Tuesday.

But the sources said it remained unclear how successful the Prudential had been. The Prudential has declined to comment. Any white knight would have to buy around 200,000 shares to thwart CE's bid by 1300 GMT today -- the new bid deadline.
By 1200 GMT, Northern's shares were trading at 637 pence, a loss of 4.0 pence, on a turnover of about 950,000 shares.
Newcastle-based Northern Electric's independence has been on a knife-edge since last Friday, when the initial bid timetable closed. CE Electric fell fractionally short of winning control.

But in an unusual twist, the Takeover Panel decided to extend the bid until 1300 GMT today because of a discretionary performance-related payment of 250,000 pounds to Northern's advisers BZW, which had not been declared until Friday.
Gallingly for Northern Electric, CE Electric had by Monday boosted shareholder acceptances for its bid to just over the 50 percent mark needed for victory from 49.77 percent on Friday.
Northern's appeal against the decision to extend the vote was thrown out by the Takeover Panel late on Monday.
Northern is not the only party to have had an attempted appeal rejected during this bitterly-contested bid battle.
The Panel last week also rejected an appeal by CE about the purchase of just over two percent of Northern's shares last week by advisers Schroders and BZW.
